text:
Maria: Heads-up — seeing a sharp p99 latency blip on shared-gpu pool `gamma` starting at ~1812500000. p50 steady, p99 jumped from ~65ms -> ~450ms for a ~6m window. correlates with a bursty tenant that got a bunch of evictions. :eyes:
PerfBot: alert: LATENCY_SPIKE detected on pool=gamma p99=450ms baseline=65ms sample_window=6m incident=INC-2026-0317-42
Kevin: Any kernel-autoswitch logs around the same time? could be expensive fallback path or non-optimal kernel chosen after eviction.
Maria: Yep — I pulled a couple traces. kernel selection changed mid-request for several samples. snippet:
```
2026-03-17T10:04:12Z trace=abc123 tenant=t-42 seq_len=1152 batch=1 kernel=mhsa_fwd_f32 -> mhsa_fwd_autoswitch_f16
latency_tokens_before: 0.9ms -> after switch: 9.1ms
KV_cache_hit: false (miss)
```
Josh: That line jump is ugly. KV miss rate spiked too? maybe cache eviction churn causing repeated regen + kernel reorder overhead.
Maria: Exactly. KV miss rate for t-42 jumped from ~12% -> ~87% during the spike window. When cache misses happen with long seqs we fall into a kernel path that isn't well-optimized for the batch/seq distribution.
Sara: Was there any preemption/autoscaler activity? I saw some pods restarted around that time in the pool.
InfraBot: event: pod_preempted namespace=redwood-runtime pool=gamma pod=serving-phi-7 reason=eviction timestamp=1812499988
Kevin: Ok — so timeline: tenant burst -> autoscaler/population churn -> KV evictions -> high miss rate -> kernel fallback/autoswitch chosen -> p99 spike.
Josh: Short-term mitigation ideas: 1) force-disable kernel-autoswitch on pool gamma 2) tighten per-tenant concurrent token caps 3) increase KV cache retention slightly to avoid cascade.
Maria: I'm leaning to (1) + (2) as fastest. (3) needs careful memory impact analysis.
Kevin: I'll prepare a canary: set env FORCE_KERNEL=mhsa_fwd_f32 for pool gamma and roll to 10% of nodes, watch p99.
Sara: I already pushed a quick rule to limit per-tenant concurrent batches to 8 on pool gamma for the next 30m. should blunt noisy neighbor.
Maria: Running a small sample probe now. Also added a trace sampler to log 'kernel_selection_reason' + 'kv_hit' for future correlation.
PerfBot: incident INC-2026-0317-42 created and paged oncall (eng-runtime). link: https://dash.redwood/internal/incidents/INC-2026-0317-42
Kevin: Can someone collect top-10 tenants by eviction rate in pool gamma for the last 24h? we need to see if this is a single offender or multi-tenant churn.
Josh: On it — querying now. quick result: t-42 responsible for 62% of eviction ops during window, t-81 and t-93 have small spikes.
Maria: Next steps: (A) temp disable autoswitch on pool gamma (Kevin will canary) (B) keep per-tenant concurrent limits (Sara) (C) postmortem + perf profile to tune fallback kernel paths and KV-resilience (Maria writing).
Kevin: Can we also add a small metric: kernel_fallback_rate and kv_miss_by_tenant so ops can alert earlier?
Maria: Yep — adding metrics + dashboard panel. I'll open a PR with the panel + brief notes.
Sara: Thanks all. if the canary looks good I'll ramp the kernel change and keep the tenant cap for 24h while we monitor. :thumbsup:
Maria: Follow-up: created PR https://git.redwood/infra/runtime/pulls/822 (adds kernel_fallback_metric, trace sample, and dashboard). I'll paste perf profiles in the PR.
PerfBot: resolved alert? No — still elevated p99 on a few nodes, but trending down after actions. next check in 15m.
Maria: Closing loop: we should treat kernel_autoswitch as 'safety-first' not performance-first when KV misses are high. longer-term we need a fallback-cost estimator in the selector (account for kv_miss probability). adding to roadmap.
Kevin: Agreed. good triage. posting postmortem + tuning plan once we have full profiles.
Maria: Thanks everyone. I'll assemble the incident notes and owners.
